finding_4.title: Conflict of Interest Act violations — 14 Entities Flagged
finding_4.summary: 14 individuals/organizations flagged under Conflict of Interest Act violations (max penalty: $500 AMPs / referral to RCMP). Public office holders must not further their private interests or those of relatives using their position. Action available: s.504 private prosecution available.

evidence.fact: Justin Trudeau: Violated 4 sections of Conflict of Interest Act. Vacationed on Aga Khan's private island — $215,000 government expenditures. Aga Khan Foundation received $50M+ federal funding. Commissioner Dawson ruled Trudeau and Aga Khan were NOT friends (30 years no contact).

Justin Trudeau: Violated Conflict of Interest Act s.9. PM and his office pressured AG Wilson-Raybould to intervene in SNC-Lavalin prosecution. Commissioner Dion: 'The authority of the Prime Minister and his office was used to circumvent, undermine and ultimately attempt to discredit the decision of the director of public prosecutions.'

Bill Morneau: Violated 3 provisions of Conflict of Interest Act — s.6(1), s.7, s.21. Failed to recuse from WE Charity grant discussions despite personal friendship with Craig Kielburger. WE employed Morneau's daughter. WE paid $41,000 in Morneau family travel expenses.

Dominic LeBlanc: Violated s.6(1) and s.21 of Conflict of Interest Act. Awarded multimillion-dollar Arctic surf clam licence to Five Nations Clam Co. — wife's first cousin Gilles Theriault involved in winning bid.

Mary Ng: Violated s.6(1) and s.21 of Conflict of Interest Act. Awarded $5,840 (2019) and $16,950 (2020) government contracts to Pomp & Circumstance PR agency, co-founded by friend Amanda Alvaro. 20-year personal friendship — vacationed together, celebrated birthdays/holidays.
Greg Fergus: Violated Conflict of Interest Act by writing letter of support for a television channel's CRTC application for mandatory carriage.

finding_8.title: Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act — 3 Entities Flagged
finding_8.summary: 3 individuals/organizations flagged under Foreign Influence Transparency and Accountability Act (max penalty: 5 years / $5M fine). Requires registration of arrangements with foreign principals. Currently UNPROCLAIMED (Day 658+). Action available: .

evidence.fact: Han Dong: CSIS believed Dong was 'witting affiliate' of China's election interference networks. Global News alleged he advised Chinese diplomat to delay releasing Michael Kovrig and Michael Spavor. 2019 nomination involved busing international students to vote.

NSICOP Unnamed Parliamentarians: NSICOP June 2024 report alleged some MPs/senators 'wittingly' helped China and India meddle in Canadian politics. Intelligence showed MPs worked on India's behalf to influence colleagues, provided confidential information to foreign officials. NSICOP alleged interference in CPC and LPC leadership races.

Pierre Poilievre: ONLY party leader to refuse security clearance to view NSICOP foreign interference report naming compromised parliamentarians. Trudeau told inquiry he saw names of Conservative parliamentarians and candidates who were 'clear risk.' 2/3 of Canadians including CPC voters said all leaders should read the report.
